title: The Simultaneous Houses

features.name: the first dwelling
features.desc-on-touch: you find yourself touching brick that remembers being timber, timber that recalls being clay; the house is not decaying, it is returning through every form it has been

features.name: the overlapping second
features.desc-on-touch: where one house ends, another has already begun; you cannot tell if they are collapsing into each other or learning to share the same walls

features.name: the keeper's vigil
features.desc-on-touch: a figure sits on a bench between the houses, facing neither one; they are counting seasons on their fingers, the count never reaching the same number twice

features.name: the third-that-was-always-there
features.desc-on-touch: behind both houses stands a structure you cannot focus on directly; each time you look away and back, it has changed slightly, the way houses change when you are not living in them

features.name: the season-nesting
features.desc-on-touch: here time has learned to stop choosing which season comes next; they all arrive at once, layered like the house-walls, each one living inside the other without contradiction

inscription: each house remembers being built and being abandoned; here they have learned to do both at once

file.name: Dwellings_Simultaneous_Register_1997-2031.txt
file.note: a local government record that has begun listing buildings by all their ages at once; each entry corrupted to include occupation details from every decade the property has existed

exits.label: back toward the shelter of nested time
toward the archive where all versions stand together
along the drift-path where ghosts learn to cohabitate
deeper into the layers where nothing moves or everything moves at once

reverie.title: REVERIE — old house, teaching time
narr: she finds you sitting on the porch step of a place
that stopped being lived-in forty years before she was born.
—time doesn't work here, you say. —no, she says,
time works here perfectly. it just stopped choosing.
you listen to the house settle, hearing decades
fold into each other like pages no one is reading.
